summary: Session-replay idempotency token encoding mismatch causing partial duplicate tool invocations across Python/TS/Go SDKs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicate external tool invocations (side effects) on a subset of streaming session-replay/ reconnect events. Behavior is inconsistent across language SDKs: Python client shows deduped behavior on most reconnects, while TypeScript and Go clients see partial duplicate function/tool executions. Impact: customer observed duplicate downstream webhooks and database writes for ~2% of streaming reconnects during high-throughput sessions. This is causing data integrity concerns for DocuServe's document-processing pipeline.

Observed pattern appears tied to the idempotency/session token encoding used by SDKs and how API gateway normalizes headers when an API key rotation or proxy rewrite occurs mid-stream.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer opens a multiplexed streaming session with a long-lived session id and uses SDK streaming + function-calling.
2) Within the session, force a transient network blip causing client reconnect and session replay (common in mobile or flaky networks).

3) During the reconnection, rotate the API key (or simulate header rewrite via proxy) so the outgoing request headers differ in base64 encoding/padding for the session token between initial and replayed frames.

4) Observe server-side dedup check: when token canonicalization fails, the server treats the replay as a new request for some shards and proceeds to invoke hosted function/webhook again, producing duplicate side effects.
5) Reproduce across python, ts, and go SDKs to see inconsistent dedup rates (python appears more resilient in existing infra).
logs: 2026-03-09T14:22:37Z INFO incoming-replay token=eyJzZXNzaW9u... (base64url no padding) client=python/1.7.8
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) - 2026-03-10: Customer provided reproducer that flips API key during an active streaming session. They see duplicate webhook posts about 2% of reconnects, impacting billing reconciliation. Asked for logs and SDK versions.

Marco Liu (Eng) - 2026-03-10: Investigating. Initial suspicion: header normalization and base64 variant (base64 vs base64url, padding) leading to non-canonical idempotency token; server dedup uses exact-match lookup. Requesting sample raw HTTP frames and SDK request header traces.

DocuServe SRE (customer) - 2026-03-11: Attached PCAP and proxy rewrite configuration. Proxy adds Accept-Encoding and rewrites small headers; base64 padded token present after proxy. Noted that Python client sends base64url without padding by default.

Marco Liu (Eng) - 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally with a tiny harness. Confirmed Python and TS produce different encodings depending on stdlib/base64 helper used when building session tokens. Filing SDK patches and server-side canonicalization change.

Marco Liu (Eng) - 2026-03-12: Rolling a server-side hotfix to canonicalize idempotency/session tokens by base64url-normalizing and stripping padding prior to dedup lookup. Will ship simultaneous SDK fixes for consistent generation. Requested short customer can apply workaround: set explicit 'Idempotency-Token' header value (hex sha256) to ensure exact-match dedup avoiding encoding differences.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: SDKs use different base64 helpers: Python uses base64.urlsafe_b64encode (no padding removal), TS uses Buffer.toString('base64') producing padded variant; Go library behavior depends on encoding used by client code. This leads to token strings that differ even when underlying bytes identical.
Hypothesis 2: Proxy or API key rotation path may re-serialize headers resulting in padding being added/removed, causing non-equal lookup keys on server side.

Reproduction: Created minimal streaming harness that toggles header rewrite mid-session. Verified dedup lookup used exact string equality. When server normalizes to base64url-without-padding, duplicates disappear in the harness.

Scope: Affects multiplexed streaming and session-replay flows where dedup relies on session tokens in headers. Observed across multiple customers but at low percent; customers with aggressive proxy rewriting or midstream API key rotation see higher rates.
Risk: Potential for more duplicates during high-reconnect scenarios until SDKs and server canonicalization land. Non-duplicated paths (where explicit idempotency header provided) are safe.

Planned fixes: (a) server hotfix to canonicalize incoming token strings before dedup lookup, (b) SDK releases to consistently generate token as base64url without padding and expose helper to set explicit hex idempotency token, (c) docs/update runbook for customers and support.
Timeline: Server hotfix staged to prod us-east 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC; SDK patches targeted for python 1.8.2, ts 2.3.1, go 0.9.7 in next release window.
resolution: Workaround: Customer instructed to set explicit Idempotency-Token header (hex sha256 of session id + nonce) for critical streams until SDK updates roll out. Server hotfix deployed to normalize base64 variants by stripping padding and using base64url canonical form during dedup lookup. SDK patches merged to generate canonical tokens. Follow-ups: Patch release notes, update streaming idempotency runbook, QA cross-language binary equivalence test added to CI.
follow_up_actions: 1) Track SDK releases and notify DocuServe when python 1.8.2, ts 2.3.1, go 0.9.7 are published.
2) Add CI job to fuzz header encodings across SDKs to prevent regressions.
3) Update public docs and runbook: canonical idempotency token guidance and recommended explicit header pattern.
4) Postmortem with incident classification if customer reports further duplicates after fixes.
